result.summary:
Independently re-checked docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-037.md against handoffs/WF02-REQ-037/step-03-test-designer.json, gh issue #69's full text/10 ACs, docs/agents/design/REQ-037.md, and the actual shipped implementation (apps/bot/src/domain/inviteCode.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/user.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/inviteCodes.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaff.ts, apps/bot/src/i18n/en.ts). All 10 ACs have at least one precise, mechanically-followable case; no TODOs found. No 'check it looks right'-style vague case anywhere in the 26 `it` blocks.

AC-by-AC verification performed:

- AC1: three `it`s (personal/bulk/companion) each read the freshly-inserted invite_codes row back via latestInviteCodeRow and assert issuedToUserId/grantsCompanionOf/maxUses exactly per the design's field-setting tables. Confirmed against domain/inviteCode.ts's issuePersonalInviteCode/issueBulkInviteCode/issueCompanionInviteCode (lines 175-314): field composition matches the test's assertions exactly.

- AC2: both cases (default expiry = event.startsAt, explicit override wins) read expiresAt back and compare .getTime(). Confirmed handlers/inviteCodes.ts's `const expiresAt = input.expiresAt ?? resolved.event.startsAt` (lines 163, 204, 251) and domain/inviteCode.ts's parseExpiresAtOverride matches the test's exact override string handling.

- AC3: seedUserWithNullTgId() inserts a `users` row DIRECTLY via `db.insert(users).values({ tgId: null, ... })` -- never through resolveOrCreateUser (which always writes a tg_id via onConflictDoUpdate on users.tgId). This genuinely constructs a pre-arrival user, not a user who has opened the bot. The case sanity-asserts `targetRowBefore.tgId` is null BEFORE issuing, then asserts the reply is 'Code issued:' and NOT catalog.inviteCodes.userNotFound. Confirmed handlers/inviteCodes.ts's makeInvitePersonalHandler calls only `userExistsById(db, input.targetUserId)` (domain/user.ts:178-181, a plain existence-by-id SELECT with no tgId condition) -- matches the design's stated behavior exactly.

- AC4: constructs an event with requiresInvite:false, requiresApproval:false, counts invite_codes before (0) and after (1) a successful /invite_bulk. Confirmed resolveEventForIssuing (handlers/inviteCodes.ts:92-128) never reads requiresInvite/requiresApproval -- matches design §2 step 5's explicit non-check.

- AC5: two `it`s, cancelled (via cancelEvent, matching its real signature `cancelEvent(db, actorUserId, eventId, chapterId, title, at)` from event.ts:666-673) and finished (endsAt in the past, exercising isFinished via evaluationTime = new Date()). Both count invite_codes before and after and assert equality (0==0), and both assert the exact catalog message (`catalog.inviteCodes.eventCancelled`/`eventFinished`) via toBe, not a substring guess.

- AC6: constructs a redeemer with a profiles row carrying BOTH a real-shaped phone (+77011234567) and email (definitely-secret@example.com) actually stored, then greps the captured detail-view reply text for the used_count fraction and name/company (must be present) and for the literal phone/email strings AND a partial-digit fragment of the phone (must be absent). Confirmed domain/inviteCode.ts's listInviteCodeRedeemers select clause (lines 434-446) structurally never selects profiles.phone/profiles.email -- the test's negative assertions have a real structural guarantee behind them, not a lucky formatting accident.

- AC7: the redeeming registration is inserted via a bare `db.insert(registrations).values(...)` call, never through any REQ-037 domain function (issuePersonalInviteCode/issueBulkInviteCode/issueCompanionInviteCode never write registrations, confirmed by reading all three -- each performs exactly one invite_codes INSERT + one writeAuditLog call, nothing else). This is the exact bypass mechanism required: REQ-037 itself never writes registrations (that's REQ-038/039 scope), so the only way to construct 'a redemption exists' without invoking not-yet-built code is a direct DB insert, which is what the case does. The case captures codeRowBefore.updatedAt, performs two detail-view reads (before and after the direct insert) confirming the second read reflects the new redeemer via the tg_username fallback (`@${redeemerTgUsername}`, confirmed against deriveCheckinDisplayName's real fallback branch at registration.ts:862-864), then re-reads the invite_codes row and asserts `codeRowAfter.updatedAt.getTime() === codeRowBefore.updatedAt.getTime()` -- a genuine bit-for-bit unchanged comparison, not merely 'still exists'. Confirmed listInviteCodeRedeemers/getInviteCodeDetail (inviteCode.ts:427-488) contain no UPDATE/INSERT/DELETE statement anywhere in the read path -- the read-only property is structural, and the test proves it operationally.

- AC8: three genuinely distinct negative cases -- (1) plain member, (2) EventStaff member added via the real addEventStaff(db, actorUserId, eventId, targetUserId, eventTitle, at) (matches eventStaff.ts:70-77's real signature exactly; EventStaff carries role='member', not organizer/owner, so it is refused by requireOrganizerForChapter's 'not-organizer' branch, not a redundant repeat of case 1), (3) an organizer of chapter A issuing for a chapter B event (refused by the 'wrong-chapter' branch). Each case counts invite_codes for the target event before (0) and re-counts after, asserting no new row, and asserts the exact `catalog.inviteCodes.notAuthorized` reply text. Confirmed handlers/inviteCodes.ts's resolveEventForIssuing returns a single uniform 'notAuthorized' reason for both requireOrganizerForChapter failure branches, matching the test's single expected message across all three cases.

- AC9: re-ran both git grep commands myself against the actual current source rather than trusting the prior report. `git grep -nE "ctx\.reply|ctx\.api\.sendMessage|bot\.api\.sendMessage|answerCallbackQuery" apps/bot/src/handlers/inviteCodes.ts` returns 22 matches, every one a bare `ctx.reply(...)`/`ctx.answerCallbackQuery(...)` call with no chat_id/recipient argument -- confirmed by reading each matched line myself, none passes targetUserId/hostUserId/issuedToUserId/grantsCompanionOf or any tgId-derived variable. `git grep -n "grammy\|Context" apps/bot/src/domain/inviteCode.ts` returns zero matches (confirmed: the file imports only node:crypto, drizzle-orm, db/schema, i18n/catalog, auditLog, registration -- no grammy symbol, no Context type anywhere). Both conditions the spec claims hold, genuinely, against real current source -- this is not a check that would pass trivially against an unrelated string; it is anchored to the exact recipient-argument absence and the exact domain-layer import list. The static-check reasoning itself is sound: 'no code path exists' is an absence-of-a-call-site property with nothing dynamic to assert against beyond enumerating every call site and inspecting each -- exactly what the grep does exhaustively (22/22 matches inspected, not sampled).

- AC10: three `it`s (personal/bulk/companion), each captures the audit_log count for the new invite_codes row (via countAuditRows keyed on entityId) and asserts it is exactly 1 with action 'invite_code.issue'. Confirmed against domain/inviteCode.ts: each of the three issue functions performs exactly one writeAuditLog call inside the same db.transaction as the INSERT, with action:'invite_code.issue' literal -- matches exactly. auditBefore is also asserted 0 (beforeEach truncates audit_log), giving a genuine before/after count as the AC requires.

tg_id range: grepped every 'let nextTgId' declaration across apps/bot/src myself (24 files found). Highest prior band confirmed at 1_031_000_000 (scheduler/autoDeclineJobs.db.test.ts). The spec's claimed 1_040_000_000+ band does not collide with any existing band.

All function signatures the spec's test code calls (resolveOrCreateUser, userExistsById, createEvent, publishEvent, cancelEvent, isFinished, getEventById, addEventStaff, issuePersonalInviteCode, issueBulkInviteCode, issueCompanionInviteCode, listInviteCodesForEvent, getInviteCodeById, getInviteCodeDetail, listInviteCodeRedeemers, parseInvitePersonalArgs/parseInviteBulkArgs/parseInviteCompanionArgs, makeInvitePersonalHandler/makeInviteBulkHandler/makeInviteCompanionHandler/makeInviteCodesListHandler/makeInviteCodeDetailCallbackHandler, INVITE_OPEN_PATTERN) were checked directly against their real, shipped implementations -- all match exactly in name, parameter order and return shape, confirming these cases exercise real functions and real handler dispatch, not aspirational ones. Catalog string keys referenced (eventCancelled, eventFinished, notAuthorized, userNotFound, detailEmpty, issuedReply's 'Code issued:' prefix) were checked against apps/bot/src/i18n/en.ts lines 343-365 and match verbatim.
